content.text: Checking the item: free trade imports = 75 - 30 = 45 (thousand); with tariff = 65 - 50 = 15. Tariff revenue = 15 × $20 = $300,000 (not $900,000). Working the item: MR = 100 - 4Q, so MR = MC gives Q = 20 and P = 60. Profit = (60-20)*20 = 800. The competitive quantity is 40, so DWL = 0.5*(60-20)*(40-20) = 400. With a $40 ceiling, the ceiling is binding and the monopolist faces a flat MR of 40 up to Q = 30, where the ceiling meets demand. Since MR 40 > MC 20, it produces 30 units. Profit = (40-20)*30 = 600.

This is a standard AP FRQ-style monopoly item with a graph. The numbers are clean and the reading load is light. The part (d) price-ceiling kink in MR is a modest conceptual step. The graphing demands (4 points in part a, with intercepts) are typical for exam-style questions.
